thread:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed on Dedicated cluster `fallow-prod` for tenant `fallow-tenant`. Error rate spike started ~5m ago. Paging on-call.
amy-oncall: on it. paging ryan-sre. What severity? any customer-visible 5xx% or just internal?
ryan-sre: seeing 5xx jump from ~0.2% -> 6.8% over the last 10m. 504s and 502s mostly at the gateway layer and some 5xx from model servers. Tail latency spiked. GPU mem pressure on a subset of nodes: memory usage at 98% on pool `dedicated-gpu-eu-3`.
ryan-sre: quick metrics snippet: 
```
5m error_rate: 6.8%
p50 latency: 210ms -> 420ms
95 latency: 1.2s -> 3.8s
gpu_mem_used: 98% on 4/12 nodes in pool
```
maria-platform: any noisy tenant patterns? Could be large batch jobs or KV thrashing. Is prefix caching eviction high?
ryan-sre: KV evictions have spiked and we see continuous batching queues growing for that tenant. Also long-running streaming sessions from the same tenant, lots of large context lengths (10k tokens) -> KV cache blowout.
amy-oncall: tagging customer-success for impact: @customer-success-alex how many requests affected?
customer-success-alex: I see elevated errors for 'Fallow Inc' API keys. Their top product endpoint is getting 503s. Rough estimate: ~12% of their requests in the window failed. I'll prep a quick note to send if we need external comms.
amy-oncall: immediate mitigation suggestions? prioritize fallbacks and protect others.
maria-platform: propose steps (short):
- throttle/limit per-tenant concurrency for fallow-tenant to safe qps
- route new requests to burst/dedicated-burst pool (if available)
- temporarily reduce default batch_size for that tenant to 1/2 and disable long-context sessions (enforce max seq len 2048)
- spin an eviction job for runaway KV entries for that tenant
- if available, switch to quantized model variant (faster mem profile)

ryan-sre: executing throttling + route now. running commands: 
```
# limit concurrent requests
redwood tenant update fallow-tenant --concurrency-limit 10
# route policy
redwood route update --tenant fallow-tenant --policy burst-capacity
```
infra-bot: `redwood route update` completed — policy applied: burst-capacity routing (2min ago).
amy-oncall: starting a gentle eviction of KV cache for that tenant: 
```
rbctl kv evict --tenant fallow-tenant --threshold 0.75 --dry-run
rbctl kv evict --tenant fallow-tenant --threshold 0.75 --execute
```
ryan-sre: applied reduced batch size for their model route: `batch_size: 4 -> 2`. Also forced model variant to `gptf-quant-8bit` for that tenant (compat check passed).
ryan-sre: monitoring now. initial metric after actions: 5xx -> 3.1%, p95 latency down to 1.6s. still above baseline but improving.
customer-success-alex: drafting message for customer: "We're seeing elevated errors on your dedicated pool due to a burst of very large requests; we've applied immediate mitigations (routing and limits) which are reducing impact. We'll follow up with a detailed post-incident summary." want to send now?
amy-oncall: hold until we see stable <1% errors, but yes prepare to send HEADS-UP. include ask: stop any large context / long streaming sessions for next 30m.
maria-platform: quick question — do we have any canary or fallback config to auto-scale the dedicated pool? Autoscaler didn't pick these nodes because GPU mem usage looked 'balanced' but cache pressure is logical. We might need a metric for kv_evictions to trigger scale.
ryan-sre: agreed. filed short ticket: `SRE-eviction-trigger` to add kv_eviction_rate ASG trigger.
amy-oncall: customers impacted: Fallow Inc production traffic for their LLM endpoint. Severity: P1 (customer-visible, partial outage). Paging escalation stays active until <1% 5xx sustained for 15m.
infra-bot: `rbctl kv evict` finished. Evicted ~22% of keys belonging to fallow-tenant; dropped memory usage on impacted nodes to ~72%.
ryan-sre: metrics now: 5xx 1.4% (10m window), p95 980ms. queues drained. GPU mem normalized for previously saturated nodes. Looks like eviction + routing + reduced batch_size did most of the heavy lifting.
amy-oncall: nice. amy-oncall: next steps:
- keep limits in place for 1h, then ramp if stable
- schedule follow-up postmortem and remediation (guardrails: per-tenant long-context caps, kv eviction alerts, autoscale trigger)
- notify customer with the prepared note but include 'please avoid long streaming sessions while we finish root cause'

customer-success-alex: sending customer note now. Copy: 
"Hi Fallow team — we detected elevated errors on your dedicated cluster and applied routing and rate limits which have reduced errors. We recommend halting long streaming/large-context requests briefly while we finish diagnostics. We'll follow up with RCA"

amy-oncall: thanks. who owns RCA? ryan-sre + maria-platform?
ryan-sre: I'll take primary for SRE side, will collect traces and request samples.
maria-platform: I'll own platform changes (autoscale trigger + limits + runbook updates).
amy-oncall: adding action items to incident tracker and closing paging when stable. Anyone want to add notes?
ryan-sre: sample log snippet showing the failure pattern: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:22:14Z] gateway: request_id=abc123 tenant=fallow-tenant status=504 backend=kv-cache reason="kv_miss_and_timeout" ctx_tokens=10240
[2026-03-15T10:22:16Z] modelserver: gpu_mem=98% request_id=abc124 seq_len=9800 queued_for=1.9s
```
amy-oncall: ack. I'll check back in 30m. If errors stay <1% for 15m straight, we'll close. Great job team. :thumbsup:
ryan-sre: adding retrospective note: tenant should be recommended a 'long-context' dedicated plan or move those requests to isolated pool.
maria-platform: I'll draft the runbook patch and a monitoring dashboard tile for kv_eviction_rate.
infra-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation steps and timeline recorded to incident-4350012345 in opsdb.
amy-oncall: closing note (provisional): service stabilized after routing + evict + batch size reduction. Follow-ups: RCA within 48h, runbook + autoscale trigger in 7d, CS follow-up with Fallow in 24h.
customer-success-alex: confirming customer acknowledged and appreciated the heads-up.
ops-bot: Incident status -> MONITORED (P1 -> MONITORING).
